chunks.text: INTERVIEW TRANSCRIPT: DEREK COLE Case: Apex Robotics Tactical Drone Crash Interviewer: Agent Vance

chunks.speaker: Derek Cole
chunks.text: Interviewee: Derek Cole, Lead Firmware Engineer [09:00 AM] VANCE: State your name and role at Apex Robotics. [09:00 AM] COLE: Derek Cole, lead embedded firmware engineer for SkyHarrier-9.

chunks.speaker: Derek Cole
chunks.text: [09:01 AM] VANCE: Did you modify the flight controller firmware before yesterday's live demonstration? [09:01 AM] COLE: Absolutely not. I approved the final stable build v2.4 at 18:00 UTC and signed off the checksum. [09:02 AM] VANCE: Where were you between 20:00 and 21:30 UTC last night?

chunks.text: [09:02 AM] COLE: I left the facility at 19:45 UTC. I was at dinner at Bistro Laurent in town until 21:30 UTC. chunks.speaker: Liam Vance
chunks.text: Interviewee: Liam Vance, QA Safety Specialist [11:45 AM] VANCE: Liam, describe the firmware validation telemetry. [11:45 AM] LIAM: Standard protocol requires two-engineer authorization before flashing firmware.

chunks.speaker: Liam Vance
chunks.text: [11:46 AM] VANCE: Did the automated build pipeline trigger an alert? [11:46 AM] LIAM: Yes. At 20:18 UTC, our QA dashboard flashed a red banner: 'MANUAL FLASH OVERRIDE DETECTED ON AIRFRAME #09'. It bypassed the standard cryptographic verification.

chunks.speaker: Elena Rostova
chunks.text: Interviewee: Elena Rostova, Chief Flight Test Pilot [10:30 AM] VANCE: Elena, what did you observe prior to the 21:00 UTC test flight? [10:30 AM] ROSTOVA: I conducted the visual pre-flight inspection of SkyHarrier-9 at 20:00 UTC. The airframe was pristine.

chunks.speaker: Elena Rostova
chunks.text: [10:31 AM] VANCE: Did you see anyone approach the drone in Hangar 3? [10:31 AM] ROSTOVA: Yes. Around 20:15 UTC, I walked back toward Assembly Bay to grab my checklist. I saw Derek Cole standing by the drone's avionics bay with a laptop and a flashing blue USB dongle. [10:32 AM] VANCE: What happened during the test flight at 21:05 UTC?

chunks.speaker: Elena Rostova
chunks.text: [10:32 AM] ROSTOVA: At altitude 400 meters, all four brushless motors cut out simultaneously. It wasn't stall or battery drain; it was an abrupt software cutoff.
